name: Spliceosome-Mediated RNA Trans-splicing (SMaRT)
therapeuticGoalDescription: Replace the mutant portion of a pre-mRNA with a corrected RNA sequence through spliceosome-mediated trans-splicing, thereby restoring production of a functional transcript and protein.
molecularDefect: Pathogenic mutations affecting coding regions where replacement of part of the transcript is preferable to transcript degradation or exon skipping.
diseaseMechanism: An engineered RNA trans-splicing molecule binds the target pre-mRNA through a binding domain and recruits the endogenous spliceosome to perform trans-splicing, replacing the mutant RNA segment with a therapeutic sequence.
suitableVariantTypes: Coding-region mutations; nonsense mutations; frameshift mutations; selected missense mutations; multi-exon pathogenic regions; mutations requiring replacement of large transcript segments.
typicalDiseases: Cystic Fibrosis (CFTR); Hemophilia A (F8); Epidermolysis Bullosa (COL7A1); Retinitis Pigmentosa (RHO/RPGR experimental); Huntington disease (experimental).
rnaTargetRegion: Target pre-mRNA intronic sequences adjacent to the intended trans-splicing site.
transcriptRequirement: Target gene must be actively transcribed to generate sufficient endogenous pre-mRNA for trans-splicing.
typicalLength: Variable; typically >1 kb, substantially longer than conventional ASOs because RTMs include therapeutic coding sequences.
designRules: Identify an efficient intronic binding site; minimize competition with endogenous cis-splicing; optimize splice donor/acceptor elements; validate corrected transcript formation by RT-PCR and sequencing; confirm restoration of protein function.
secondaryStructureRequirement: Accessible pre-mRNA binding regions are preferred; excessive secondary structure can reduce RTM binding and trans-splicing efficiency.
offTargetConsiderations: Off-target trans-splicing; aberrant chimeric transcripts; unintended splice junctions; competition with endogenous splicing.
advantages: Can replace large mutant transcript regions; mutation-independent within the replaced segment; preserves endogenous gene regulation.
limitations: Generally low trans-splicing efficiency; competition with cis-splicing; complex vector delivery; no approved clinical therapies.

evidenceLevel.rating: Moderate (extensive preclinical evidence, no approved therapy).
